pointers.sentence: A `Signer` takes keyword arguments only (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.__init__`).

`Signer.__init__` raises `ValueError` for a separator that is empty or made only of the characters of URL-safe base64 and its padding: letters, digits, `"-"`, `"_"` and `"="` (`django/core/signing.py:_SEP_UNSAFE`).
`Signer.sign` returns the value, the separator and the signature (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.sign`).

`Signer.signature` passes the signer's salt followed by `"signer"`, the value, the signer's key (or one passed to it) and its algorithm to `base64_hmac`, which writes in URL-safe base64 the HMAC that `salted_hmac` makes of the value under a key derived from that salt and key ([Secret keys and `django.utils.crypto`](keys.md)) (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.signature`, `django/core/signing.py:base64_hmac`).

`Signer.signature` passes the signer's salt followed by `"signer"`, the value, the signer's key (or one passed to it) and its algorithm to `base64_hmac`, which writes in URL-safe base64 the HMAC that `salted_hmac` makes of the value under a key derived from that salt and key ([Secret keys and `django.utils.crypto`](keys.md)) (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.signature`, `django/core/signing.py:base64_hmac`).
`Signer.unsign` reverses `Signer.sign` (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.unsign`).

A signer given no keys reads both settings when it is made, not when it is used: one made before a change of `SECRET_KEY` goes on checking with the old key, and one made after the change refuses what the old key signed unless the old key is among its fallbacks (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.__init__`).
`dumps`, `loads` and `get_cookie_signer` make a new signer at each call (`django/core/signing.py:dumps`, `django/core/signing.py:loads`, `django/core/signing.py:get_cookie_signer`).

`TimestampSigner.timestamp` is the current time in whole seconds since the epoch, written in base 62 by `b62_encode`, with the digits and letters of `BASE62_ALPHABET` (`django/core/signing.py:b62_encode`).

`TimestampSigner.sign` appends the separator and the timestamp to the value before passing it to `Signer.sign`, so the signature covers the time as well (`django/core/signing.py:TimestampSigner.sign`).

It splits off the timestamp and decodes it with `b62_decode`, and if given a maximum age, as seconds or a timedelta, raises `SignatureExpired` when more seconds than that have passed (`django/core/signing.py:TimestampSigner.unsign`).

An age is counted from the whole second that `TimestampSigner.timestamp` wrote, so it runs ahead of the time since signing by the fraction of a second that `timestamp` dropped (`django/core/signing.py:TimestampSigner.timestamp`).
`Signer.sign_object` signs a value of any type its serializer can write, not only a string (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.sign_object`).

It serializes the value to bytes, with `JSONSerializer` unless given another serializer class, writes them in URL-safe base64 without the `"="` padding (`django/core/signing.py:b64_encode`), and signs that with `sign`, which on a `TimestampSigner` adds the time.

`Signer.unsign_object` calls `unsign` first, passing a maximum age on to a `TimestampSigner`, and only then looks for the `"."`, decodes the base64 and decompresses: nothing unverified is ever decompressed (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.unsign_object`).
`JSONSerializer` writes JSON with no space after a comma or a colon and encodes it as Latin-1 (`django/core/signing.py:JSONSerializer`).
The default serializer is JSON so that even a stolen `SECRET_KEY` does not let an attacker run commands on the server, as forged data read with the pickle format could (`docs/topics/signing.txt`).

`dumps` makes a `TimestampSigner` from its key and salt and returns its `Signer.sign_object` of the value; `loads` makes one from its key, salt and fallback keys and returns its `Signer.unsign_object` of the string (`django/core/signing.py:dumps`, `django/core/signing.py:loads`).

Within Django the sessions call them, for a session's data and, in the backend that keeps the session in its cookie, for the session key ([The session store: `SessionBase`](../auth/sessions.md), [The session backends](../auth/session-backends.md)) (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.encode`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/signed_cookies.py:SessionStore._get_session_key`).

A salt is a namespace: a string signed under one does not verify under another, so a value the site signed for one use cannot be passed to code that checks for another (`docs/topics/signing.txt`).
Leaving the salt of `dumps` at its default, or sharing one salt between different parts of an application without good cause, is for that reason a security risk (`django/core/signing.py:dumps`).
`get_cookie_signer` makes the signer for cookies (`django/core/signing.py:get_cookie_signer`).
